cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Make the Choice Rewrite the Past
cards.instruction: Make them choose between options whose consequences reinterpret an earlier promise, refusal, or agreement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Choose the overseas job or running this shop with me. I'm going to know what your 'we'll build something' promised.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said that before the job offer arrived.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then decide what survives the offer. Stay, and I'll call it a promise to work beside me. Go, and I'll call it encouragement you gave me to work alone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're turning a job into a goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose what you're saying goodbye to. I'll keep the shop either way, but I'm not keeping your name on our plan while you decide what it meant.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 imposes a job/shop choice; A3 dictates what each outcome makes the old promise mean; A5 controls whether B name remains on their plan after B calls it goodbye.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2 changed timing with two present interpretations; A5 uses B4 goodbye language to demand which shared undertaking ends.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains the new offer and B4 objects to emotional framing, plausible independent aspirations.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 goodbye concern to make plan attribution conditional instead of abandoning the original promise dispute.

specificity.evidence: A1 overseas work versus running shop and A5 shared plan provide concrete stakes; no romantic status required.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 two interpretations are long but necessary; A5 plan-name consequence anchors otherwise literary goodbye language.
